question:
Assertion: There is high reactiviy seen in two extremes of the periodic table and lowest in the centre.

Reason: The ionization enthalpy of the extreme left element in a period is the highest and the electron gain enthalpy of the element on the extreme right is the least negative.
answer: Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
explanation: The atomic and ionic radii, as we know, generally decrease in a period from left to right. As a consequence, the ionization enthalpies generally increase (with some exceptions as outlined in section 3.7.1(a)) and electron gain enthalpies become more negative across a period. In other words, the ionization enthalpy of the extreme left element in a period is the least and the electron gain enthalpy of the element on the extreme right is the highest negative (note : noble gases having completely filled shells have rather positive electron gain enthalpy values). This results into high chemical reactivity at the two extremes and the lowest in the centre. Thus, the maximum chemical reactivity at the extreme left (among alkali metals) is exhibited by the loss of an electron leading to the formation of a cation and at the extreme right (among halogens) shown by the gain of an electron forming an anion.(Reference- NCERT Chemistry Class 11 (Part 1); Page 94; Paragraph no. 2)
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> Classification of elements and periodicity in properties >> Periodic Trends and Chemical reactivity
option_a: Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation for assertion.
option_b: Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
option_c: Assertion and reason both are correct statements and reason is correct explanation for assertion.
option_d: Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.

question: What is the basic difference between the terms electron gain enthalpy and electronegativity?
answer: Property of bonded atom vs isolated atom
explanation:
The basic difference between the terms electron gain enthalpy and electronegativity is property of bonded atom vs isolated atom, because Electron gain enthalpy is the tendency of an isolated gaseous atom to accept an additional electron to form a negative ion. 

Electronegativity is the tendency of the atom of an element in a chemical compound to attract a shared pair of electrons towards it in a covalent bond.

question: The element expected to form the largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is
explanation:
In isoelectronic species, as the negative charge increases, the size of the ion also increases. 
Step 1: 
The noble gas configuration of a given element is as follows:

Na when lose one electron and form Na+ then it obtained a noble gas configuration.
O when gain two electrons and form O2- then it obtained a noble gas configuration. 
F when gain one electron and form F- then it obtained a noble gas configuration. 
N when gain three electrons and form N3- then it obtained a noble gas configuration. 

Step 2: 
Na+ , O2-, F-,  and N3- are isoelectronic species. In the case of isoelectronic species, as the negative charge increases, the size of the ion also increases. 

Thus, N3- has the largest size and Na+ has the minimum size. 

Thus, option fourth is the correct answer. Reference: (Class-11)(NEET2023)

question: The correct order of least negative to most negative electron gain enthalpy for C,Ca,Al,F,and O:
explanation:

During the addition of an electron, energy can either be released or absorbed.Electron gain enthalpy becomes more negative along the period. This is because the effective nuclear charge increases from left to right and it will be easier to add an electron to a smaller atom.
Also, it becomes less negative down the group because size of the atom increases and the added electron will be farther from the nucleus.So, the order of least negative to most negative electron gain enthalpy will be: Ca < Al < C < O < F .

question: Incorrect order among the following
explanation:

Thus, acidic character decreases as we move from NH3  to AsH3.

question: The first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al and Si are in the order
explanation:
The electronic configurations of Na and Mg are:
Na (11): [Ne] 3s1 and Mg (12): [Ne] 3s2 In both
 the atoms, the electron is to be removed from 3s-orbital but nuclear 
charge in Na is less than Mg. Thus, ionisation energy of Na is less than
 Mg (Na < Mg).

The electronic configurations of Mg and Al are:

Mg: [Ne] 3s2; Al: [Ne] 3s2 3pl

In Mg, the electron is to be removed from 3s-orbital while in Al, 
it is to be removed from 3p-orbital. Since it is easier to remove an 
electron from 3p-orbital in comparison to 3s-orbital, the ionization 
enthalpy of Mg is higher than Al (Mg > Al).

The electronic configurations of Al and Si are:

Al (13): [Ne] 3s2 3p1 Si (14): [Ne] 3s2 3p2

In both the atoms, the electron is to be removed from 3p-orbital 
but nuclear charge in Si is more than Al. Thus, ionisation enthalpy of 
Al is less than Si

question: The electronic configuration of gadolinium (Atomic number 64) is
explanation:
The electronic configuration of La (Z = 57) is [Xe] 5dl 6s2.
 Therefore, further addition of electrons occurs in the lower energy 
4f-orbital till it is exactly half-filled at Eu (Z = 63) Thus, the 
electronic configuration of Eu is [Xe] 4f7 6s2. Thereafter, addition of next electron does not occur in the more stable exactly half-filled 4f7 shell but occurs in the little higher energy 5d-orbital. Thus, the electronic configuration of Gd (Z = 64) is [Xe] 4f7 5dl 6s2.

question:
Electronic configurations of four elements A, B, C and D are given below :
(A) 1s2 2s2 2p6                          

(B) 1s2 2s2 2p4

(C) 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1                  

(D) 1s2 2s2 2p5
Which of the following is the correct order of increasing tendency to gain electron :
explanation:
A – Is2 2s2 2p6 – Noble gas configuration
B -1s2 2s2 2p4 – 2 electrons short of stable configuration
C – 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1 – Requires one electron to complete 5-orbital
D -1s2 2s2 2p5 – Requires one electron to attain noble gas configuration
Noble gases have no tendency to gain electrons since all their  orbitals are completely filled. Thus, element A has the least electron  gain enthalpy.
Since element D has one electron less and element B has two electrons less than the corresponding noble gas configuration, hence,  element D has the highest electron gain enthalpy followed by element B.Since, element C has one electron in the 5-orbital and hence needs  one more electron to complete it, therefore, electron gain enthalpy of C is less than that of element B. Combining all the facts given above, 
the electron gain enthalpies of the four elements increase in the order A  < C < B < D.

than adding an electron to the larger 3p-orbital. Hence the element with most negative electron gain enthalpy is chlorine; the one with the least negative electron gain enthalpy is phosphorus.
(NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Page 87 Box Problem 3.7)

question: Which of the following statements justifies the prediction of the first ionization enthalpy value for Al?
answer: Al has a higher nuclear charge than Si, indicating a higher ionization enthalpy.
explanation: The first ionization enthalpy is the energy required to remove the most loosely held electron from an atom in the gaseous state. This means that it takes more energy to remove an electron from an atom with a higher nuclear charge because the attraction between the positively charged nucleus and the negatively charged electron is stronger.In the given question, the ionization enthalpy of Mg (737 kJ/mol) is higher than that of Na (496 kJ/mol) because Mg has a higher nuclear charge than Na. Similarly, Si has a higher nuclear charge than Al, so it is expected that the ionization enthalpy of Al will be higher than that of Si.Therefore, the correct option is C) Al has a higher nuclear charge than Si, indicating a higher ionization enthalpy.(NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Page 86 Box Problem 3.6)

Reason: The Law of Triads works only for a few elements.
answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and the Reason is a correct explanation of the Assertion.
explanation:
The Law of Triads was a classification system proposed by the German chemist Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner in 1829, which stated that certain groups of three elements had similar chemical and physical properties, and that the middle element's atomic weight was approximately equal to the average of the other two.

However, the Law of Triads was later dismissed as a coincidence because it did not hold true for all elements, and it was difficult to find similar triads for many elements.

question: Which of the following is not true for drug receptors

question: _____________ only control symptoms not cause of over production of HCL.
explanation: Over production of acid in the stomach causes irritation and pain. In severe cases, ulcers are developed in the stomach. Until 1970, only treatment  for  acidity was administration of antacids, such as sodium hydrogencarbonate or a mixture of aluminium and magnesium hydroxide. However, excessive hydrogencarbonate can make the stomach alkaline and trigger the production of even more acid. Metal hydroxides are better alternatives because of being insoluble, these do not increase the pH above neutrality. These treatments control only symptoms, and not the cause. Therefore,  with these metal salts, the patients cannot be treated easily. In advanced stages, ulcers become life threatening and its only treatment is removal of the affected part of the stomach.(Reference: NCERT Chemistry Class 12; Page 451; Paragraph No. 2)

3. Antibiotics effective against a single organism or disease, they are referred to as limited spectrum antibiotics.

question:
Which statement is true:
 
 a)Tranquilizers relieve anxiety, stress, irritability or excitement by inducing a sense of well-being.
 
 b) Iproniazid is derivative of barbituric acid.
 
 c)chlordiazepoxide and meprobamate, are relatively mild tranquilizers suitable for relieving tension.
explanation:
Tranquilizers are a class of chemical compounds used for the treatment of stress, and mild or even severe mental diseases. These relieve anxiety, stress, irritability or excitement by inducing a sense of well-being.
 
 Derivatives of barbituric acid viz., veronal, amytal, nembutal, luminal and seconal constitute an important class of tranquilizers. These derivatives are called barbiturates.
 
 Some tranquilizers namely, chlordiazepoxide and meprobamate, are relatively mild tranquilizers suitable for relieving tension.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 444 paragraph 2)

question:
Which statement is false 
 
 a)Analgesics reduce or abolish pain although they may cause impairment of consciousness, mental confusion, incoordination or paralysis or some other disturbances of nervous system.
 
 b)Aspirin and paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics.
 
 c)Morphine produce sleep.
explanation:
Analgesics reduce or abolish pain without causing impairment of consciousness, mental confusion, incoordination or paralysis or some other disturbances of nervous system.
 
 Aspirin and paracetamol belong to the class of non-narcotic analgesics. Aspirin is the most familiar example. Aspirin inhibits the synthesis of chemicals known as prostaglandins which stimulate inflammation in the tissue and cause pain.
 
 Morphine and many of its homologues, when administered in medicinal doses, relieve pain and produce sleep.
 
 (Reference NCERT Class 12 page 445 paragraph 1)

question:
Which statement is true 
 
 a)Tranquilizers and analgesics affect the message transfer mechanism from nerve to receptor.
 
 b)If the level of noradrenaline is low for some reason,antidepressant drugs are required.
 
 c)Equanil is used in controlling depression and hypertension.
explanation:
Tranquilizers and analgesics are neurologically active drugs. These affect the message transfer mechanism from nerve to receptor.
 
 If the level of noradrenaline is low for some reason, then the signal-sending activity becomes low, and the person suffers from depression. In such situations, antidepressant drugs are required.
 
 Some tranquilizers namely, chlordiazepoxide and meprobamate, are relatively mild tranquilizers suitable for relieving tension. Equanil is used in controlling depression and hypertension.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 444 paragraph 2)

question:
Which statement is correct?
 
 a)Aspirin inhibits the synthesis of prostaglandins which stimulate inflammation in the tissue and cause pain.
 
 b)Opiates are obtained from the opium poppy.
 
 c)Morphine narcotics, n poisonous doses, these produce stupor, coma, convulsions and ultimately death.
explanation:
Aspirin inhibits the synthesis of chemicals known as prostaglandins which stimulate inflammation in the tissue and cause pain. These drugs are effective in relieving skeletal pain such as that due to arthritis.
 
 Morphine narcotics are sometimes referred to as opiates, since they are obtained from the opium poppy. 
 
 These analgesics are chiefly used for the relief of postoperative pain, cardiac pain and pains of terminal cancer, and in child birth.
 
 Morphine and many of its homologues, when administered in medicinal doses, relieve pain and produce sleep. In poisonous doses, these produce stupor, coma, convulsions and ultimately death.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 445 paragraph last)

 b)An antimicrobial tends only to destroy microbes such as bacteria (antibacterial drugs), fungi (antifungal agents), virus (antiviral agents).
 
 
 c)Antibiotics are used as drugs to treat infections because of their low toxicity for humans and animals.
explanation:
An antimicrobial tends to destroy/prevent development or inhibit the pathogenic action of microbes such as bacteria (antibacterial drugs), fungi (antifungal agents), virus (antiviral agents), or other parasites (antiparasitic drugs) selectively.
 
 Antibiotics are used as drugs to treat infections because of their low toxicity for humans and animals.
 
 Heroine is a morphine drug.

question:
Which statement is false
 
 
 a)antibiotics were classified as chemical substances produced by microorganisms.
 
 
 b)An antibiotic now refers to a substance produced wholly or partly by chemical synthesis, which very high concentrations inhibits the growth or destroys microorganisms.
 
 c)arsphenamine is most effective treatment discovered for syphilis.
explanation:
Antibiotics are used as drugs to treat infections because of their low toxicity for humans and animals. Initially antibiotics were classified as chemical substances produced by microorganisms (bacteria, fungi and molds) that inhibit the growth or even destroy microorganisms.
 
 
 
 An antibiotic now refers to a substance produced wholly or partly by chemical synthesis, which in low concentrations inhibits the growth or destroys microorganisms by intervening in their metabolic processes.
 
 
 
 Arsphenamine, known as salvarsan.was the first effective treatment discovered or syphilis. Although salvarsan is toxic to human beings, its effect on the bacteria, spirochete.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 446 paragraph last)

explanation:
Ehrlich succeeded in preparing the first effective antibacterial agent, prontosil, which resembles in structure to the compound, salvarsan.
 
 Antibiotics have either cidal (killing) effect or a static (inhibitory) effect on microbes.
 
 The range of bacteria or other microorganisms that are affected by a certain antibiotic is expressed as its spectrum of action.

 Penicillin G has a narrow spectrum.
 
 Chloramphenicol, isolated in 1947, is a broad spectrum antibiotic. It is rapidly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and hence can be given orally in case of typhoid, dysentery, acute fever...

 c)Liquid dishwashing detergents are ionic type detergent.

Cetyltrimethylammoniumbromide is a popular cationic detergent and is used in hair conditioners.
 
 Liquid dishwashing detergents are non-ionic type of detergent.

Cationic detergents are quarternary ammonium salts of amines with acetates, chlorides or bromides as anions. Cationic part possess a long hydrocarbon chain and a positive charge on nitrogen atom. Hence, these are called cationic detergents.
 
 In anionic detergents, the anionic part of the molecule is involved in the cleansing action. Sodium salts of alkylbenzenesulphonates are an important class of anionic detergents. They are mostly used for household work. Anionic detergents are also used in toothpastes.

question:

 b)histamine causing the inflammation of the body is example of classification on the basis on drug action
 
 c)analgesics having pain killing effect,is an example of classification based on drug action
explanation:
This classification is based on pharmacological effect of the drugs. It is useful for doctors because it provides them the whole range of drugs available for the treatment of a particular type of problem. For example, analgesics have pain killing effect, antiseptics kill or arrest the growth of microorganisms.
 
 It is based on the action of a drug on a particular biochemical process. For example, all antihistamines inhibit the action of the compound, histamine which causes inflammation in the body.

question:
Which statement is correct?
 
 a)Enzymes are example, proteins which perform the role of biological catalysts in the body.
 
 b)The first function of an enzyme is to hold the substrate for a chemical reaction.
 
 c)The second function of an enzyme is to provide functional groups that will attack the substrate and carry out chemical reaction.
explanation:
In their catalytic activity, enzymes perform two major functions:
 
 The first function of an enzyme is to hold the substrate for a chemical reaction. Active sites of enzymes hold the substrate molecule in a suitable position, so that it can be attacked by the reagent effectively.Substrates bind to the active site of the enzyme through a variety of interactions such as ionic bonding, hydrogen bonding, van der Waals interaction or dipole-dipole interaction 
 
 The second function of an enzyme is to provide functional groups that will attack the substrate and carry out chemical reaction.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 440 paragraph last)

question:

 a)Drugs inhibit any activities of enzymes.
 
 b)Drugs that compete with the natural substrate for their attachment on the active sites of enzymes are called competitive inhibitors.
 
 c)Allosteric site is not a site on the enzyme
explanation:
Drugs inhibit any of the above mentioned activities of enzymes. These can block the binding site of the enzyme and prevent the binding of substrate, or can inhibit the catalytic activity of the enzyme. Such drugs are called enzyme inhibitors.
 
 Drugs compete with the natural substrate for their attachment on the active sites of enzymes. Such drugs are called competitive inhibitors.
 
 Some drugs do not bind to the enzyme’s active site. These bind to a different site of enzyme which is called allosteric site.
 
 (Reference NCERT class 12 page 441 paragraph last)

question:

 c)Message between two neurons and that between neurons to muscles is communicated through chemical messengers.

 In the body, message between two neurons and that between neurons to muscles is communicated through certain chemicals. These chemicals, known as chemical messengers are received at the binding sites of receptor proteins.

question:

Reason (R) Receptors are proteins.

explanation:
Receptors are specialized proteins found on the surface or inside cells that are crucial to the body's communication process. They receive and transmit signals from hormones, neurotransmitters, and other signaling molecules, allowing cells to respond and adapt to changes in their environment.

The reason that receptors are proteins is also true. Receptors are typically made up of amino acids and have a specific three-dimensional structure that enables them to recognize and bind to their specific ligands or signaling molecules.

However, while the reason is true, it does not provide a complete explanation for the assertion. While it is true that receptors are proteins, the fact that they are proteins alone does not fully explain why they are crucial to the body's communication process. The complex nature of receptor signaling and their role in cellular communication is what makes them crucial to the body's overall function.

question:
Which of the following is a correct statement.
 
 i. Laws of thermodynamics apply only when a system is in equilibrium state.
 
 ii. Laws of thermodynamics apply only when a system moves from one equilibrium state to another equilibrium state.
 
 iii. Laws of thermodynamics deal with energy changes of macroscopic system only
 
 iv. First law of thermodynamics, ∆U = q + w
explanation:
i. This statement is incorrect because the laws of thermodynamics are applicable to both equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems.

ii. This statement is also incorrect because the laws of thermodynamics are applicable to all processes, not just those that involve a system moving from one equilibrium state to another.

iii. This statement is partially correct. The laws of thermodynamics deal with energy changes of both microscopic and macroscopic systems. However, they are mainly concerned with macroscopic systems because the behavior of microscopic systems is described by statistical mechanics.

iv. This statement is correct. The first law of thermodynamics, also known as the law of conservation of 
energy, states that the change in the internal energy (∆U) of a system is equal to the heat added to the system (q) plus the work done on the system (w).

(Reference: NCERT chemistry class 11; Page 154; Paragraph No.1)

 Assertion : The enthalpy change for the reaction CaO(s) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) is called enthalpy of formation of calcium carbonate.

The magnitude of the coefficient depends
on the size, composition and nature of the

explanation:
w = -Pex.dv, w = -5 ×5.6 = -28.0J. Because this work is used an raising the temperature of water, 
so work done is equal to the heat supplied i.e.,  w = m.Cs..∆T
Given that, m = 18g (=1 mole), Cs = 4.184J/g/K, q = +28.0J, ∆T = ?(Heat is given to water)
∆T = q/Cs.m = 28.0/4.184 ×18 = 0.371

 Which of the above formula is false?

question: Why enthalpy of neutralization is less if either the acid or the base or both are weak?

depends on the strength of the intermolecular
interactions in the substance undergoing the
phase transfomations. For example, the strong
hydrogen bonds between water molecules hold
them tightly in liquid phase. For an organic
liquid, such as acetone, the intermolecular
dipole-dipole interactions are significantly
weaker. Thus, it requires less heat to vaporise
1 mol of acetone than it does to vaporize 1 mol
of water.

R = 8.314 × 10^-3 kJ/K/mol, T = 300 K

∆U = ∆H - ∆ngRT = (-78.84kJ) - (1 mol) × (8.314 × 10^-3 kJ/K/mol) × 300 K
= - 81.35 kJ

question:
Consider the following statements of bond enthalpy: 
 
 i. Chemical reactions involve the breaking and making of chemical bonds. 
 
 ii. Physical reactions involve the breaking and making of chemical bonds. 
 
 iii. In diatomic molecules, the enthalpy of atomization is also the bond dissociation enthalpy. 
 
 iv. The bond dissociation enthalpy is the change in enthalpy when one mole of covalent bonds of a gaseous covalent compound is broken to form products in the solid phase. 
 
 Which of the following statements is correct?
explanation:
Chemical reactions involve the breaking and
making of chemical bonds. Energy is required
to break a bond and energy is released when
a bond is formed. It is possible to relate heat
of reaction to changes in energy associated
with breaking and making of chemical bonds. 
 In case of diatomic molecules, like
dihydrogen the enthalpy of change involved in this process is the
 bond dissociation
enthalpy.  
The bond dissociation enthalpy is the change
in enthalpy when one mole of covalent bonds
of a gaseous covalent compound is broken to
form products in the gas phase.i. This statement is correct. Chemical reactions typically involve the breaking of existing chemical bonds in reactants and the formation of new chemical bonds in products.

iii. This statement is correct. In diatomic molecules, the bond dissociation enthalpy is equal to the enthalpy of atomization. Bond dissociation enthalpy refers to the energy required to break a particular bond in one mole of a gaseous substance, and in diatomic molecules, breaking the bond also results in the formation of two separate atoms.

iv. This statement is correct. The bond dissociation enthalpy is defined as the enthalpy change when one mole of covalent bonds in a gaseous covalent compound is broken to form products in the solid phase. It is a measure of the strength of a particular covalent bond.
(Reference: NCERT chemistry class 11; Page 171; Paragraph No.6.5)

question:
Consider the following statements of spontaneity: 
 
 i. A spontaneous process is an irreversible process and may only be reversed by some external agency. 
 
 ii. A spontaneous process is an reversible process and may only be reversed by some external agency. 
 
 iii. All naturally occurring processes whether chemical or physical will tend to proceed spontaneously in one direction only. 
 
 iv. In spontaneous reaction, reaction occuring in extremely slow rate. 
 
 Which of the following statements is correct?
explanation:
Take the case of combination of
hydrogen and oxygen. These gases may be
mixed at room temperature and left for many
years without observing any perceptible
change. Although the reaction is taking place between them, it is at an extremely slow rate.
It is still called spontaneous reaction. So
spontaneity means ‘having the potential to
proceed without the assistance of external
agency’. However, it does not tell about the
rate of the reaction or process. 
A spontaneous process is an irreversible process and may only  be reversed by some external agency.

question: Calculate the standard enthalpy change of burning methane ? ΔHf°(CO2) = -393,5kJ/mol, ΔHf°(H2O) = - 241,8 kJ/mol, ΔHf°(CH4) = - 74,9 kJ/mol.
explanation:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of methane (CH4) is:

CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O

The enthalpy change for this reaction can be calculated using Hess's law, which states that the enthalpy change of a reaction is equal to the sum of the enthalpy changes of its individual steps.

Step 1: Calculate the enthalpy change for the formation of one mole of CH4 from its constituent elements:

C(graphite) + 2H2(g) -> CH4(g) ΔHf° = -74.9 kJ/mol

Step 2: Calculate the enthalpy change for the combustion of one mole of CH4 to form one mole of CO2 and two moles of H2O:

CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(l) ΔH° = ?

To calculate the enthalpy change for this step, we need to use the enthalpy of formation values for CO2 and H2O, as well as the enthalpy of formation of CH4 calculated in Step 1. We can use the following equation:

ΔH° = ΣΔHf°(products) - ΣΔHf°(reactants)

where ΣΔHf° represents the sum of the standard enthalpies of formation for each product or reactant, with the coefficients of the balanced chemical equation taken into account.

ΔH° = [ΔHf°(CO2) + 2ΔHf°(H2O)] - ΔHf°(CH4)
ΔH° = [(-393.5 kJ/mol) + 2(-241.8 kJ/mol)] - (-74.9 kJ/mol)= -802.26 kJ/mol
 
 (Reference: NCERT class 11 page 170 paragraph last)

The greater the disorder in an isolated system, the higher is the entropy.

Whenever heat is added to the system, it increases molecular motions causing increased randomness in the system.

For a given substance, the crystalline solid state is the state of lowest entropy (most ordered).

question:
Consider the following:

(a) The stability of hydrides decreases from NH₃ to BiH₃. 
(b) The reducing character of the hydrides increases down the group.
(c)  Ammonia is a strong reducing agent. 
(d) BiH₃ is the strongest reducing agent amongst all the hydrides. 

Which of the following options are correct?
explanation:
Reactivity towards hydrogen: All the elements of Group 15 form hydrides of the type EH₃ where E = N, P, As, Sb or Bi. The hydrides show regular gradation in their properties. The stability of hydrides decreases from NH₃ to BiH₃ which can be observed from their bond dissociation enthalpy. Consequently, the reducing character of the hydrides increases. Ammonia is only a mild reducing agent while BiH₃ is the strongest reducing agent amongst all the hydrides.
(Reference: (NCERT Chemistry Class 12; Page No. 173; Paragraph No.2)

question: What is the order of basicity?

explanation:
PCl₅  is used in the synthesis of some organic compounds, e.g.,C₂H₅Cl, CH₃COCl. In gaseous and liquid phases, PCl₅  has a trigonal bipyramidal structure. question: The molecular shape shown in diagram(n2109)
explanation:
The central atom Br has seven electrons in the valence shell. Three of these will form electron pair bonds with three fluorine atoms leaving behind four electrons. Thus, there are three bond pairs and two lone pairs. According to VSEPR theory, these will occupy the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. The two lone pairs will occupy the equatorial positions to minimise lone pair-lone pair and the bond pair lone pair repulsions which are greater than the bond pair-bond pair repulsions. In addition, the axial fluorine atoms will be bent towards the equatorial fluorine in order to minimise the lone-pair-lone pair repulsions. The shape would be that of a slightly bent ‘T’.
(Reference' (NCERT Chemistry Class 12 Page No. 207 Paragraph No. 4)

question: Which one of the following arrangements does not give the correct picture of the trends indicated against it?
answer: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂ : Bond dissociation energy
explanation:
In case of diatomic molecules (X₂) of halogens the bond dissociation energy decreases in the order : Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂. This is due to relatively large electron-electron repulsion among the lone pairs is F₂ than in case of Cl₂. The oxidising power, electronegativity and reactivity decrease in the order : F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂ Electron gain enthalpy of halogens follows the given order : Cl₂ > F₂ > Br₂ > I₂ The low value of electron gain enthalpy of fluorine is probably due to small size of fluorine atom.
(Reference' (NCERT Chemistry Class 12 Page No. 198 Table 7.8)
(AIPMT 2008)

question: The reaction that is a part of large scale industrial preparation of nitric acid is: Refer diagram (214303Q)
explanation:
The Ostwald process is a chemical process used for making nitric acid (HNO3). It is a mainstay of the modern chemical industry, and it provides the main raw material for the most common type of fertilizer production.
 
(i) Ammonia is converted to nitric acid in 2 stages. It is oxidized by heating with oxygen in the presence of a catalyst such as Pt with 10% Rh, Pt metal on fused silica wool, Cu or Ni, to form NO and water (as steam).
This reaction is strongly exothermic, making it a useful heat source once initiated.
 (ii) Stage two encompasses two reactions and is carried out in an absorption apparatus containing water. Initially nitric oxide is oxidized again to yield nitrogen dioxide.

This gas is then readily absorbed by the water, yielding the desired product (nitric acid, albeit in a dilute form), while reducing a portion of it back to nitric oxide
(NEET 2022)

question: Which one of the following statements is not true?
answer: HF is a stronger acid than HCl.
explanation:
1. Iodine has the highest electrode potential value and thus is the weakest oxidising agent or the strongest reducing agent.
2. Fluorine exhibits only -1 oxidation state whereas other halogens show +1, +3, +5 and +7 oxidation states also. Fluorine being the most electronegative element cannot have positive oxidation state.

Other halogens have d orbitals, therefore can expand their octet.

3. In Group 17 oxyacids, electron density is drawn away from the O atom as the electronegativity of the halogen increases. This in turn draws electron density away from the O–H bond and weakens it.

The weaker the O–H bond, the stronger the acid. Cl is more electronegative than Br so,  HOCl is stronger acid than HOBr.

4. Amongst the haloacids, only HF is weak. Acid strength can be determined by the stability of the conjugate base (for most acids, the conjugate base is what you get when you remove H+ from the acid).

Stability of conjugate base : I- >Br- > Cl-  >F-

Acidity order: HF < HCl < HBr < HI

Thus, HCl is stronger acid than HF
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> The p-Block Elements >> Previous year questions
option_a: Among halide ions, iodide is the most powerful reducing agent.
option_b: Fluorine is the only halogen that does not show a variable oxidation state.
option_c: HOCl is a stronger acid than HOBr.
option_d: HF is a stronger acid than HCl.

question: Choose the incorrect statement among the following regarding noble gases
answer: Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points
explanation:
The general electronic configuration of noble gas elements is ns2 np6 except He (i.e. 1s2).

Noble gases have large positive electron gain enthalpy because the extra electron has to be placed in the next higher principal quantum energy level thereby producing a highly unstable electronic configuration.

Noble gases only have London dispersion forces, so there's very little attraction between water and these noble gases. They still can dissolve, but only very little, because some water molecules will be able to form dipole-induced dipole attractions with the noble gas atom.

Because of weak dispersion forces melting point and boiling points of noble gases are low.

The melting and boiling point (respectively) of noble gas is as follows: 

Ne= 24.6 K; Ar= 83.8 K; Kr=115.9 K; Xe=161.3 K; Rn=202 K

He=4.2 K; Ne=27.1 K; Ar=87.2 K; Kr=119.7 K; Xe=165.0 K; Rn=211 K

question: In which Nitrogen oxide both the N-O bonds are not equal?
explanation:
In N₂O and NO, there is only one N-O bond. In NO₂, both the N-O bonds are equal as both of them participate equally in resonance. Likewise in N₂O₄ there are 4 N-O bonds and all of them are equal due to their participation in resonance. However in N₂O₃ there are 3 N-O bonds out of which on 2 N-O bonds participate in resonance. Therefore there are 2 bonds with partial double bond character and 1 bond with complete double bond character. In N₂O₅, there are 6 N-O bonds out of which 4 have partial double bond character due to resonance and 2 have single bond because of forming bridged structure with central oxygen. Thus N₂O₃ and N₂O₅ have different N-O bond lengths.
(Reference' (NCERT Chemistry Class 12 Page No. 178 Paragraph No. 7.4)

explanation:

question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Electron gain enthalpy values for O → O⁻ and O → O²⁻ as –141 and 702 kJ/mol respectively, There is the formation of a large number of oxides having O²⁻ species and not O⁻

Reason (R) : The lattice energy of O²⁻ is much lower than the lattice energy of O⁻

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
explanation:
Oxygen has negative first electron gain enthalpy and positive second ionization enthalpy . Based on this, we should expect the formation of oxides with O⁻ species and not with O²⁻  species. However, in reality, most oxides have O²⁻ ion due to following reasons:
(i) O²⁻ has stable noble gas electronic configuration.
(ii) The lattice energy of O²⁻  is much higher than the lattice energy of O⁻.This more than compensates the higher energy required for removal of second electron from O⁻ to form O²⁻ and makes O²⁻ ion stable.

answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
explanation:
Cl is more electronegative (and smaller in size) than Br. Hence, the tendency of Cl to withdraw electrons from Cl-O-H bond is higher than the tendency of Br to withdraw electrons from Br-O-H bond. question: On addition of conc. H2SO4 to a chloride salt, colourless fumes are evolved but in case of iodide salt, violet fumes come out. This is because
explanation:
The reason why colourless fumes are evolved on addition of concentrated H2SO4 to chloride salt and violet fumes come out in case of iodide salt is due to the difference in the nature of the halides and the reaction that occurs when they are treated with H2SO4.When concentrated H2SO4 is added to a chloride salt, it reacts with the chloride ion to form HCl gas, which is a colourless gas.
 The reaction is as follows:NaCl + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HCl .The HCl gas formed on reaction with H2SO4 is a strong acid and can react with moisture in the air to form white fumes of hydrochloric acid.On the other hand, when concentrated H2SO4 is added to an iodide salt, it reacts with the iodide ion to form hydrogen iodide gas (HI), which is a violet coloured gas. The reaction is as follows:NaI + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HIThe hydrogen iodide gas formed on reaction with H2SO4 is a weak acid and gets oxidized to form iodine, which gives the violet fumes. The oxidation of HI to iodine is due to the strong oxidizing power of concentrated H2SO4, which acts as an oxidizing agent in this reaction.Reference: NCERT Chemistry Part II textbook for class 12, Chapter 7, p. 276.
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> The p-Block Elements >> NCERT Exemplar Questions

question: In qualitative analysis when H2S is passed through an aqueous solution of salt acidified with dil. HCl, a black precipitate is obtained. On boiling the precipitate with dil. explanation: The given question is related to the qualitative analysis of a salt solution using hydrogen sulfide gas, dilute hydrochloric acid, dilute nitric acid, and ammonia.When hydrogen sulfide gas is passed through an aqueous solution of a salt acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid, a black precipitate is obtained. This black precipitate is due to the formation of insoluble sulfides of certain metals like lead, copper, silver, mercury, etc.On boiling the black precipitate with dilute nitric acid, it forms a blue-colored solution. This blue coloration is due to the formation of nitro complexes of metals like copper and lead.Addition of an excess of aqueous solution of ammonia to this blue solution gives a deep blue solution of copper tetrammine complex. This is because ammonia forms complex ions with metal ions like Cu2+ to form tetrammine copper complexes.References: NCERT Chemistry Part II textbook for class 12, Chapter 6, p. 242-243.

question: Which of the following elements can be involved in pπ–dπ bonding?
explanation: pπ-dπ bonding is a type of covalent bonding in which both p orbitals and d orbitals of two atoms overlap and form a bond. This type of bonding is seen in compounds of phosphorus, such as phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5), phosphorus pentoxide (P4O10), etc. In these compounds, the central phosphorus atom has five unpaired electrons in its valence shell, which can hybridize to form five sp3d orbitals. Four of these sp3d orbitals are used to form four sigma bonds with chlorine/oxygen atoms, while the remaining sp3d orbital overlaps with the p orbital of the other phosphorus atom to form a pπ-dπ bond.On the other hand, carbon and nitrogen typically form covalent bonds through the overlap of p orbitals to form pi (π) bonds, whereas boron usually forms three covalent bonds with other atoms using its three valence electrons in its p orbital.Reference: NCERT Chemistry Part II textbook for class 12, Chapter 7, p. 268-270.
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> The p-Block Elements >> NCERT Exemplar Questions

question: In XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆ the number of lone pairs on Xe are respectively [2002]
explanation:
In XeF₂, Xe has two fluorine atoms attached to it, and each fluorine atom contributes one electron to form a covalent bond with xenon. Therefore, there are no lone pairs on Xe in XeF₂.

In XeF₄, Xe has four fluorine atoms attached to it, and each fluorine atom contributes one electron to form a covalent bond with xenon. Therefore, there are two lone pairs on Xe in XeF₄.

In XeF₆, Xe has six fluorine atoms attached to it, and each fluorine atom contributes one electron to form a covalent bond with xenon. Therefore, there is only one lone pair on Xe in XeF₆.

So, the correct answer is 3,2,1: XeF₂ has 0 lone pairs on Xe, XeF₄ has 2 lone pairs on Xe, and XeF₆ has 1 lone pair on Xe.

question: In case of nitrogen, NCl₃ is possible but not NCl₅ while in case of phosphorus, PCl₃ as well as PCl₅ are possible. It is due to [2002]
answer: availability of vacat d orbitals in P but not in N
explanation:
Electronic configuration of nitrogen (N) is 1s²2s²2p³, which means that it has no vacant d orbitals to accommodate the additional electrons required for the formation of NCl₅. On the other hand, phosphorus (P) has the electronic configuration of 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³, which means that it has three vacant d orbitals that can accommodate additional electrons, allowing for the formation of PCl₅.

Therefore, the availability of vacant d orbitals in P but not in N is the reason why P can form both PCl₃ and PCl₅, while N can only form NCl₃ but not NCl₅.
(Reference: (NCERT Chemistry Class 12; Page No. 165)

question: Oxidation number of Cl in CaOCl₂ is
answer: +1 and -1 since it contains ClO- and Cl-
explanation:
The oxidation number of an element in a compound is the charge it would have if all the shared electrons were assigned to the more electronegative atom in the bond.

In CaOCl2, the oxidation number of calcium (Ca) is +2 because it is a Group 2 element, and the oxidation number of oxygen (O) is -2 because it is more electronegative than calcium.

To determine the oxidation number of chlorine (Cl), we can use the fact that the sum of the oxidation numbers in a compound is equal to the overall charge of the compound. In this case, CaOCl2 is neutral, so the sum of the oxidation numbers must be zero.

Let x be the oxidation number of Cl in CaOCl2. Then we have:

+2 (from Ca) + (-2) (from O) + x (from Cl) = 0

Simplifying this equation, we get:

x = 0 - (+2) - (-2) = 0

This means that the oxidation number of Cl in CaOCl2 is zero.

However, if we consider the polyatomic ion ClO- that is present in the compound, the oxidation number of Cl in ClO- is -1 (since oxygen has an oxidation number of -2). Therefore, there must be another Cl atom with an oxidation number of +1 in order to balance the overall charge of the compound. Hence, the oxidation number of Cl in CaOCl2 is both +1 and -1, due to the presence of both ClO- and Cl- ions in the compound.
(Reference' (NCERT Chemistry Class 12 Page No. 203 Paragraph 4)
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> The p-Block Elements >> JEE Mains

question: Which one of the following substances has the highest proton affinity ? [2003]
explanation:
Proton affinity refers to the tendency of a substance to attract and bond with a proton (H+). The higher the proton affinity of a substance, the more likely it is to accept a proton.

Among the given options, NH3 (ammonia) has the highest proton affinity. This is because it has a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom, which can readily bond with a proton to form NH4+ (ammonium ion). This reaction is exothermic, releasing energy in the form of heat, which further indicates that NH3 has a high proton affinity.

question: Which among the following factors is the most important in making fluorine the strongest oxidizing halogen?[2004]
explanation:
The strength of an oxidizing agent depends on its ability to accept electrons from other substances, which in turn depends on various factors such as ionization energy, electron affinity, and bond dissociation energy.

Among the given options, bond dissociation energy is the most important factor in making fluorine the strongest oxidizing halogen. Bond dissociation energy refers to the energy required to break a bond between two atoms. Fluorine has the highest bond dissociation energy among all the halogens, meaning that it requires the most energy to break the F-F bond. As a result, fluorine can easily remove electrons from other substances and act as a strong oxidizing agent.

question:
Choose the incorrect statement regarding concentration of ores:

b. If either the ore or the gangue is attracted towards magnetic field, then the separation is carried out by magnetic separation method.
c. Froth floatation method is used for removing gangue from sulphide ores.
d. Leaching is often used if the ore is soluble in some suitable solvent.
explanation: Hydraulic washing is based on the difference between specific gravities of the ore and the gangue particles. It is therefore a type of gravity separation. Magnetic separation is based on differences in magnetic properties of the ore components. If either the ore or the gangue is attracted towards magnetic field, then the separation is carried out by this method. Froth floatation method is used for removing gangue from sulphide ores. Leaching is often used if the ore is soluble in some suitable solvent.  (Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 153-154 paragraph 3)

a. Calcination and roasting involves heating.
b. If the ore contains iron, it is mixed with silica before heating. 
c. The sulphide ores of copper are heated in blast furnace.
explanation: Calcination involves heating.Calcination removes the volatile matter which escapes leaving behind the metal oxide. In roasting, the ore is heated in a regular supply of air in a furnace at a temperature below the melting point of the metal.The sulphide ores of copper are heated in reverberatory furnace. If the ore contains iron, it is mixed with silica before heating. (Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 155 Paragraph 3 )
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> General principles and processes of isolation of Elements >> Extraction of crude metals from concentrated ore

question:
Choose the correct statement:
a. Reduction of the metal oxide usually involves heating it with a oxidizing agent.
b. The reducing agent combines with the oxygen of the metal oxide.
c. Some metal oxides get reduced easily while others are very difficult to be reduced. In any case, heating is required.
explanation: Reduction of the metal oxide usually involves heating it with a reducing agent, for example C, or CO or even another metal. The reducing agent (e.g., carbon) combines with the oxygen of the metal oxide. Some metal oxides get reduced easily while others are very difficult to be reduced (reduction means electron gain by the metal ion). In any case, heating is required. (Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 155 Paragraph 3 )
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> General principles and processes of isolation of Elements >> Extraction of crude metals from concentrated ore

question: Why in the formation of oxides, ∆S tend to be negative?
answer: Because of decrease of molecular randomness

2xM(s) + O2(g) → 2MxO(s)

(Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 158 paragraph 2).

question: Why is the reduction of a metal oxide easier if the metal formed is in liquid state at the temperature of reduction?
explanation: The entropy is higher if the metal is in liquid state than when it is in solid state. The value of entropy change (∆S) of the reduction process is more on positive side when the metal formed is in liquid state and the metal oxide being reduced is in solid state. Thus the value of ∆rG becomes more on negative side and the reduction becomes easier. (Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 159 example 6.2)
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> General principles and processes of isolation of Elements >> Thermodynamic principles of metallurgy

Cathode: Cu2+ + 2e– → Cu (6.51)

question:
Which statemant is true 
 
 a)Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from iron slag revealed evidence of continuous smelting in Khasi Hills of Meghalaya.
 
 b)India was the first country to master copper distillation.
 
 c)The remnants of former iron-ore excavation and iron manufacturing are visible even now in the landscape of Khasi Hills.
 
 d)The slag layer, which is dated to 353 BCE – CE 128, indicates that Khasi Hill region is the earliest iron smelting site studied in the entire region of North East India.
explanation:
Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from iron slag revealed evidence of continuous smelting in Khasi Hills of Meghalaya. The slag layer, which is dated to 353 BCE – CE 128, indicates that Khasi Hill region is the earliest iron smelting site studied in the entire region of North East India. The remnants of former iron-ore excavation and iron manufacturing are visible even now in the landscape of Khasi Hills. British naturalists who visited Meghalaya in early 19th century described the iron industry that had developed in the upper part of the Khasi Hills. There is archaeological evidence of zinc production in Rajasthan mines at Zawar from the 6th or 5th BCE. India was the first country to master zinc distillation.
(Reference: NCERT class 12,unit 6,page 151 paragraph 2)

explanation:
There is archaeological evidence of zinc production in Rajasthan mines at Zawar from the 6th or 5th BCE. India was the first country to master zinc distillation. Due to low boiling point, zinc tends to vapourise while its ore is smelted. Pure zinc could be produced after a sophisticated ‘downward’ distillation technique in which the vapour was condensed in a lower container. This technique was also applied to mercury. Indian metallurgists were masters in this technique. This has been described in Sanskrit texts of 14th century.

question: Brine is electrolysed by using inert electrodes. The reaction at anode is ......... Refer diagram(n0605)
explanation:
The possible reactions occurring at the anode during the electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution) using inert electrodes are:

Cl⁻(aq) → 1/2Cl₂(g) + e⁻ ; E° = -1.36 V
2H₂O(l) → O₂(g) + 4H⁺(aq) + 4e⁻ ; E° = -1.23 V
According to the standard electrode potential values, the oxidation of chloride ions has a more negative E° value than the oxidation of water molecules. Therefore, the oxidation of chloride ions to chlorine gas is thermodynamically favored over the oxidation of water to oxygen gas.

However, the kinetic factors also play an important role in determining the product of electrolysis. The oxidation of water molecules to oxygen gas is a relatively slow process compared to the oxidation of chloride ions to chlorine gas. This means that even though the oxidation of water has a higher standard electrode potential, it occurs at a slower rate than the oxidation of chloride ions.

As a result, during the electrolysis of brine, even though water molecules theoretically should get oxidized at the anode, the oxidation of chloride ions is preferred because it occurs more rapidly. Hence, chlorine gas is produced instead of oxygen gas at the anode.
topic_name: Inorganic chemistry >> General principles and processes of isolation of Elements >> Exemplar Questions

question: In the metallurgy of aluminium ............
answer: graphide anode is oxidised to carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide
explanation:
In the metallurgy of aluminum, the electrolysis is performed in a steel vessel lined with carbon. The cathode is made of carbon, while the anode is made of graphite. During the electrolysis process, aluminum ions (Al3+) are reduced at the cathode to form aluminum metal (Al), while the graphite anode is oxidized to produce carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO).

The chemical reaction occurring during this process is represented as:

2Al2O3 + 3C → 4Al + 3CO2 + 2CO

This process is known as the Hall-Heroult process. The electrolytic reactions at the cathode and anode are as follows:

At the cathode: Al3+ + 3e- → Al (reduction reaction)

At the anode: C (graphite) + O2- → CO2 + 4e- (oxidation reaction)
2C (graphite) + O2- → 2CO (oxidation reaction)

The oxidation state of oxygen changes from -2 to 0 during the oxidation reactions occurring at the anode, where oxygen combines with carbon to form CO and CO2. However, the overall reaction involved in the process does not involve a net change in the oxidation state of oxygen.

Hence, during the electrolysis of aluminum, aluminum ions are reduced at the cathode to form aluminum metal, while graphite anode is oxidized to produce carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide.

 (Reference: NCERT  , class 12 , unit 6 , page 163 paragraph 1)

question:
In the extraction of aluminium by Hall-Heroult process, purified Al2O3 is mixed with CaF2 to

(a) lower the melting point of Al2O3

(b) increase the conductivity of molten mixture.

(c) reduce Al3+ into Al(s)

(d) acts as catalyst
explanation:
In the Hall-Heroult process for the extraction of aluminum, Al2O3 is mixed with cryolite (Na3AlF6) and calcium fluoride (CaF2) to form a molten electrolyte. The addition of cryolite and calcium fluoride serves two main purposes:

(a) Lower the melting point of Al2O3: The melting point of pure Al2O3 is very high (around 2050°C), which makes it difficult and energy-intensive to melt it. However, by adding cryolite and calcium fluoride, the melting point of the mixture is lowered to around 950°C, which reduces the energy requirements for the process.

(b) Increase the conductivity of the molten mixture: The addition of cryolite and calcium fluoride also increases the conductivity of the molten mixture, allowing for the flow of electrical current through the electrolyte. This is essential for the electrolysis process, as it allows for the reduction of Al3+ ions into aluminum metal at the cathode.

Therefore, the correct options are (a) and (b). Options (c) and (d) are incorrect. Calcium fluoride does not directly reduce Al3+ ions into aluminum metal, and it does not act as a catalyst in the process.

question:
In which of the following method of purification, metal is converted to its volatile compound which is decomposed to give pure metal?

(a) Heating with stream of carbon monoxide
(b) Heating with iodine
(c) Liquation
(d) Distillation
explanation:
The method of purification in which a metal is converted into its volatile compound, which is then decomposed to obtain pure metal is known as the "vapour phase refining" method. This method is based on the principle that the metal is converted into a volatile compound, which can be purified by distillation and then decomposed to get pure metal.

Out of the given options, option (a) "heating with a stream of carbon monoxide" is an example of vapour phase refining method. This method is used for refining metals such as nickel by the Mond process. In this process, nickel is heated with a stream of carbon monoxide to form volatile nickel carbonyl (Ni(CO)4), which is then decomposed at a higher temperature to obtain pure nickel.

Option (b) "heating with iodine" is an example of the van Arkel method, which is used for refining metals such as zirconium and titanium. In this method, the metal is heated with iodine to form a volatile metal iodide, which is then decomposed to obtain pure metal.

Option (c) "liquation" is a method used for the purification of metals such as tin and lead, where the impurities are removed by selective melting and solidification.

Option (d) "distillation" is a general method used for the purification of liquids or volatile substances, and it is not specific to metal purification.
(Reference: NCERT class 12 , unit 6 , page 165 , paragraph last)

question:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) A depressant prevents certain type of particle to come to the froth.

(b) Copper matte contains Cu2S and ZnS.

(c) The solidified copper obtained from reverberatory furnace has blistered appearance due to evolution of SO2 during the extraction.

(d) Zinc can be extracted by self-reduction.
explanation:
Statement (a) is true. A depressant is a reagent that is added during froth floatation to prevent certain types of particles from coming to the froth. For example, in the separation of lead sulfide (PbS) and zinc sulfide (ZnS), sodium cyanide (NaCN) is added as a depressant to prevent ZnS from coming to the froth.

Statement (b) is false. Copper matte is a mixture of copper sulfide (Cu2S) and iron sulfide (FeS), but it does not contain zinc sulfide (ZnS).

Statement (c) is true. During the extraction of copper from its sulfide ore, the solidified copper obtained from the reverberatory furnace has a blistered appearance due to the evolution of sulfur dioxide (SO2) gas. This gas is formed as a result of the reaction between copper sulfide and oxygen.

Statement (d) is false. Zinc cannot be extracted by self-reduction. Zinc is extracted from its ore, zinc blende (ZnS), by roasting the ore in the presence of excess air to form zinc oxide (ZnO). The zinc oxide is then reduced to zinc metal using carbon. The overall reaction can be represented as follows:

ZnS + 2O2 → 2ZnO + 2SO2
ZnO + C → Zn + CO2

question:
In the extraction of chlorine from brine ............

(a) ΔG for the overall reaction is negative.
(b) ΔG for the overall reaction is positive.
(c) ΔE for the overall reaction has negative value.
(d) ΔE for the overall reaction has positive value.
explanation:
The extraction of chlorine from brine involves electrolysis, where an electric current is passed through a brine solution (sodium chloride dissolved in water) to separate the sodium and chlorine ions. The overall reaction is as follows:

2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g) + Cl2(g)

The standard free energy change (ΔG°) for this reaction is positive, which means the reaction is non-spontaneous under standard conditions. However, the reaction can be made to occur by supplying electrical energy to the system. This also means that the standard potential (E°) of the reaction is negative, since ΔG° = -nFE°, where n is the number of electrons transferred and F is the Faraday constant.

So the correct answers are (b) ΔG for the overall reaction is positive and (c) ΔE for the overall reaction has negative value.

The nickel carbonyl is then decomposed at high temperatures (~460 K) to release pure nickel metal and carbon monoxide gas.
The assertion (A) is true because nickel can indeed be purified by Mond's process. The reason (R) is also true because Ni(CO)4 is a volatile compound that decomposes at ~460 K to give pure nickel metal and carbon monoxide gas. Therefore, reason (R) is a correct explanation of assertion (A).

explanation:
The van Arkel method is a process used to purify certain metals, including zirconium. The method involves the formation and decomposition of a volatile metal iodide compound, which allows for the separation of impurities from the desired metal. The steps involved in the van Arkel method for zirconium purification are as follows:

Zirconium is heated with iodine to form zirconium tetraiodide (ZrI4).
Zirconium tetraiodide is heated to a high temperature (~1800 K) under reduced pressure, causing it to decompose into pure zirconium metal and iodine gas.
The zirconium metal is then collected and purified further by remelting and casting into ingots.
The assertion (A) is true because zirconium can indeed be purified by the van Arkel method. The reason (R) is also true because ZrI4 is a volatile compound that decomposes at a high temperature of ~1800 K, which allows for the extraction of pure zirconium metal. Therefore, reason (R) is a correct explanation of assertion (A).

So the correct answer is: Both assertion and reason are true, and reason is a correct explanation of assertion.

explanation:
Zone refining is  a very useful method for producing high-purity semiconductors. In this method, a small region of a rod-shaped material, typically a metal or semiconductor, is melted using an external heat source. The molten zone is then moved along the rod, either by pulling the rod through a stationary heater or by moving the heater along the rod.

The impurities in the material are preferentially distributed in the molten zone, and as the zone moves along the rod, these impurities are removed from the region of interest. The solidified zone that is left behind is of higher purity than the original material, and this process can be repeated several times to achieve very high levels of purity.

The assertion (A) is true because zone refining is indeed a very useful method for producing semiconductors of high purity. The reason (R) is also true because semiconductors do indeed require high levels of purity to function effectively. 

The main reason why zone refining is useful for producing high-purity semiconductors is that this method allows for precise control over the distribution of impurities in the material. This, in turn, allows for the removal of impurities from the material and the production of a highly pure final product.

question: After opening a soda water bottle, some of dissolved CO₂ fizzes out. What do you conclude?
explanation: When a soda water bottle is opened, some of the carbon dioxide gas dissolved in it fizzes out rapidly. The phenomenon arises due to  difference in solubility of carbon dioxide at different pressures. There is equilibrium between the molecules in the gaseous state and the molecules dissolved in the liquid under pressure i.e., CO₂ (gas) = CO₂ (in solution) This equilibrium is governed by Henry’s law, which states that the mass of a gas dissolved in a given mass of a solvent at any temperature is proportional to the pressure of the gas above the solvent. This amount decreases with increase of temperature. The soda water bottle is sealed under pressure of gas when its solubility in water is high. As soon as the bottle is opened, some of the dissolved carbon dioxide gas escapes to reach a new equilibrium condition required for the lower pressure, namely its partial pressure in the atmos. question:

explanation:
Initial amount of H₂O = 1 mol = 18g. 
If 40% of water by mass reacts with CO, then the amount of H₂O consumed =18×40100=7.2g=0.4mol 
So, the amount of H₂O that remains equilibrium =1−0.4 = 0.6 mol 
As per the reaction, 0.4 mol of H₂O reacts with equal amount of CO(g) and forms 0.4 mol of each of H₂ and CO₂. 
So, in the equilibrium mixture, [H₂O] = 0.6 / 10 mol⋅L −¹= 0.06 mol⋅L−¹ 
[CO] = (1−0.4) / 10 mol⋅L−¹ = 0.06 mol⋅L−¹ 
and [H₂] = [CO₂] = 0.4 / 10 mol⋅L−¹= 0.04 mol⋅L−¹ 
hence, for the reaction 
Kc=[H₂][CO₂] / [H₂O][CO]=(0.04×0.04)/(0.06×0.06) = 0.44;   Exercise question - 7.14,(NCERT chemistry class 11; page 233)

question: C (s) + CO₂ (g) = 2CO (g). At 1127 K and 1 atm pressure, a gaseous mixture of CO and CO₂ in equilibrium with soild carbon has 90.55% CO by mass .Calculate Kc for this reaction at the above temperature.
explanation:
Suppose the mixture has 100g as total mass.

The masses of CO and CO₂​ are 90.55g and 100−90.55 = 9.45 g respectively.
The number of moles of CO are 90.55/ 28 ​= 3.234.
The number of moles of CO₂​ are 9.45 / 44 ​= 0.215.
The mole fraction of CO is 3.234​ /(3.234 + 0.215 ) = 0.938.
The mole fraction of CO₂​ is 1−0.938 = 0.062.

The partial pressure of CO is the product of the mole fraction of CO and the total pressure.
It is 0.938×1 = 0.938 atm.

The partial pressure of CO₂ is 0.062 × 1=0.062 atm.

The expression for the equilibrium constant is: 
Kp​= (pCO)²​​/pCO₂​​=(0.938)²​ / 0.062 = 14.19
n ​= 2−1 = 1
Kc​=Kp​(RT)⁻ⁿ = 14.19×(0.0821×1127)⁻¹ = 0.153   ; Exercise question - 7.23,(NCERT chemistry class 11; page 234)

question: The value of Kc for the reaction 3O₂ (g) = 2O₃ (g) is 2.0 ×10⁻⁵⁰ at 25°C. If the equilibrium concentration of O₂ in air at 25°C is 1.6 ×10⁻², what is the concentration of O₃?

[O₃]² = (2.0×10⁻⁵⁰)×(1.6 ×10⁻²)³ = 8.192×10⁻⁵⁶
Hence, the equilibrium concentration of ozone is
[O₃] = 2.86×10⁻²⁸ M

question: Equal volumes of 0.002 M solutions of sodium iodate and cupric chlorate are mixed together. Will it lead to precipitation of copper iodate? (For cupric iodate Ksp = 7.4 × 10⁻⁸ ).

question: In liquid-gas equilibrium, the pressure of vapours above the liquid is constant at
explanation:

question:

SO₃(g) ⇌ SO₂(g) + 1/2O₂(g)
explanation:
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) ;K =278 . For the reverse reaction 
2SO₃(g) ⇌ 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g)  ;K' = 1/278 ......(1)
For the required reaction we can divide (1) by a value of 2 . Hence we get 
SO₃(g) ⇌ SO₂(g) + 1/2O₂(g) ;K'' = √K' , that is √(1/278)
On solving we get 
√(1/278) = 0.0599 ≈ 6 ×10⁻²

question: For the reaction N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) , the equilibrium constant is K₁. The equilibrum constant is K₂  for the reaction 2NO(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)  . What is the K for the reaction, NO₂(g) ⇌  1/2N₂(g) + O₂(g)?

NO₂(g) ⇌ NO(g) + 1/2O₂(g) ;K₂' = 1/(K₂)¹⸍² .....(ii)
On adding (i) and (ii) we get NO₂(g) ⇌  1/2N₂(g) + O₂(g) ; K' = 1/(K₁ K₂)¹⸍²

question:
Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations :

A. 60 mL M/10 HCl + 40 mL M/10 NaOH

B. 55 mL M/10 + HCl 45 mL M/10 NaOH

C. 75 mL M/5 HCl + 25 mL M/5 NaOH

D. 100 mL M/5 HCl +100 mL M/5 NaOH

pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
explanation:
For acid base mixture
if equivalence of acid > equivalence of base then the mixture is acidic .
if equivalence of acid < equivalence of base then the mixture is basic.
if equivalence of acid = equivalence of base then the mixture is neutral.
For finding that we need to find the difference of equivalence of acid and base
Generally N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ = (Valency factor x M₁)V₁ -(Valency factor x M₂)V₂ = NᵢVᵢ {Since normality = molarity  x valency factor)
Here 
A. 60 mL M/10 HCl + 40 mL M/10 NaOH 
N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ ; =((1/10 x 0.06) - (1/10 x 0.04)) =Nᵢ x 0.1 
 Nᵢ = 0.002/0.1 = 0.02 = 2 x 10⁻²
pH = -log[H+] ; [H+] = Normality 
Hence pH = -log 2 x 10⁻² = 1.698

B. 55 mL M/10 + HCl 45 mL M/10 NaOH
N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ ; =((1/10 x 0.055) - (1/10 x 0.045)) =Nᵢ x 0.1
 Nᵢ = 0.001/0.1 = 0.01 =10⁻²
pH = -log[H+] ; [H+] = Normality 
Hence pH = -log 10⁻² = 2

C. 75 mL M/5 HCl + 25 mL M/5 NaOH
N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ ; =((1/5 x 0.075) - (1/5 x 0.025)) =Nᵢ x 0.1
 Nᵢ = 0.01/0.1 = 0.1 =10⁻¹
pH = -log[H+] ; [H+] = Normality 
Hence pH = -log10⁻¹ = 1

D.100 mL M/5 HCl +100 mL M/5 NaOH
N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ ; =((1/5 x 0.1) - (1/5 x 0.1)) =Nᵢ x 0.1
 Nᵢ = 0/0.1 = 0
pH = 7 ; neutral .

question: What is the pH of the resulting solution when equal volumes of 0.1 M NaOH and 0.01 M HCl are mixed?

we know for a mixture of acid and base N₁V₁ -N₂V₂ = NᵢVᵢ and [H+] is given by resultant normality Nᵢ
Here 0.1 M NaOH and 0.01 M HCl are mixed 
1 mole of a acid is completely neutralised by 1 mole of a base
Hence 0.01 M of HCl is completely nneutralised by 0.001M NaOH ;That means 0.09M NaOH is left

0.1 x V - 0.01 x V = Nᵢ x (2V) 
0.09/2 = Nᵢ = 0.045 = [OH-] {since here base is excess and not acid therefore [OH-]}
pOH = -log[OH-] ;[OH-] = Nᵢ

pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 1.35 = 12.65

question: If A + B ⇋ C + D (Constant = K1) and E + F ⇌ G + H (Constant = K2), then what is the constant of reaction for C + D + E + F ⇒ product?
explanation:
To determine the equilibrium constant for the overall reaction, we need to combine the given equilibrium reactions in a way that yields the desired product. Here's how we can achieve this:

 Reverse the first reaction:
C + D ⇋ A + B (Constant = 1/K1)

 Add the reversed first reaction to the second reaction:
C + D + E + F ⇋ A + B + G + H (Constant = 1/K1 * K2)

 Remove common terms from both sides:
C + D + E + F ⇒ G + H (Constant = 1/K1 * K2)

 Invert the constant:
C + D + E + F ⇒ product (Constant = K1 * K2)

 Therefore, the equilibrium constant for the overall reaction C + D + E + F ⇒ product is K1 * K2.
topic_name: Physical Chemistry >> Equilibrium >> Previous Year Question

question: Which of the following species behaves as a Lewis acid?
explanation:
Analysis of options:
Stannous chloride (SnCl2): While Sn can accept a lone pair, its tendency is weaker compared to BF3. Additionally, SnCl2 readily undergoes hydrolysis in water, complicating its Lewis acid behavior.
Stannic chloride (SnCl4): Sn in SnCl4 has no empty orbitals and is surrounded by electronegative Cl atoms, making it an electron pair donor (Lewis base) rather than an acceptor.
Boron trifluoride (BF3): BF3 has only three F atoms bonded to B, leaving an empty p orbital on B. This empty orbital readily accepts electron pairs, making it a strong Lewis acid.
 Therefore, based on the definition and analysis, only BF3 exhibits the characteristics of a Lewis acid.

question:
If we drop some radioactive sugar into a beaker of saturated normal sugar solution which of the following are true?

(i)Radioactivity can be observed after sometime due to dynamic nature of equilibrium.

(ii)We see radioactivity since there is an exchange of radioactive and non-radioactive sugar molecules at the interphase.

(iii)Radioactivity is observed which stops after sometimes.

(iv)No radioactivity is observed because we are adding radioactive sugar to saturated solution.

(v)The exchange of radioactive and non radioactive sugar molecules takes place at interphase but the amount never attains a constant value.
answer: (i) and (ii) are true (iii) (iv) and (v) are false
explanation: In a saturated solution, a dynamic equilibrium exits between the solute molecules in the solid state and in the solution: Sugar (solution) Sugar (solid), and the rate of dissolution of sugar = rate of crystallization of sugar. Equality of the two rates and dynamic nature of equilibrium has been confirmed with the help of radioactive sugar. If we drop some radioactive sugar into saturated solution of non-radioactive sugar, then after some time radioactivity is observed both in the solution and in the solid sugar. Initially there were no radioactive sugar molecules in the solution but due to dynamic nature of equilibrium there is exchange between the radioactive and non -radioactive sugar molecules between the two phases. The ratio of the radioactive to non- radioactive molecules in the solution increase till it attains a constant value.(NCERT chemistry class 11; page 195 ; paragraph 1 and 2).
topic_name: Physical Chemistry >> Equilibrium >> Most challenging questions
option_a: (i),(ii) and (iii) are true (iv) and (v) are false
option_b: (i),(ii) and (iv) are true (iii) and (v) are false
option_c: (i) and (ii) are true (iii) (iv) and (v) are false
option_d: (i) and (v) are true (ii) (iii) and (iv) are false.

A(s) ⇌B(g) + C(g)  ;Kₚ₁= x atm

D (s) ⇌ C(g) + E (g) ;Kₚ₂= y atm

→P₁(P₁ + P₂) + P₂(P₁ + P₂) = x + y
→(P₁ + P₂)² = x + y  
→ P₁ + P₂ = √x+y

Total pressure = 2(P₁ + P₂) = 2 √x+y ) atm at
 equilibrium

question:
For the reaction N₂0₄(g) ⇌2N0₂(g), the value of K is 50 at 400 K and 1700 at 500 K. Which of the following options is correct?
(a) The reaction is endothermic.
(b) The reaction is exothermic.
(c) If NO₂(g) and N₂0₄(g) are mixed 400 K at partial pressures 20 bar and 2 bar respectively, more N₂0₄(g) will be formed.
(d) The entropy of the system increases.
explanation:
(a) As the value of K increases with increase of temperature and K = Kբ / K_b, this means that Kբ increases, i.e., forward reaction is favoured.
Hence, reaction is endothermic.
(c)  At 400K , Q = P²_NO₂/P_N₂0₄ = (20)²/2 = 200. Thus Q>K . Equilibrium will shift backwards to form more N₂0₄.

question:

Given Kₛₚ for
FeS = 6.3 × 10⁻¹⁸,
MnS = 2.5 × 10⁻¹³,
ZnS = 1.6 × 10⁻²⁴ and
CdS = 8.0 × 10⁻²⁷.
explanation:
Precipitation will take place in the solution for which ionic product is greater than solubility product. As 10 mL of solution containing S²⁻ ion is mixed with 5 mL of metal salt solution, after mixing

[S²⁻]=1.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ x10/15= 6.67 × 10⁻²⁰
[Fe²⁺] = [Mn²⁺] = [Zn²⁺] = [Cd²⁺]=(5/15)0.04 =1.33× 10⁻². 

Hence the ionic product [M²⁺][S²⁻] = 1.33 x 10² x 6.67 x 10⁻²⁰ = 8.87 x 10⁻²² 
Therefore in ZnS (K = 1.6 x 10²⁴) and CdS (Ksp = 8.0 × 10⁻²⁷), ionic product exceeds solubility product. Hence, precipitation will take place

question: The ionization constant of benzoic acid is 6.46 × 10⁻⁵ and Kₛₚ for silver benzoate is 2.5 × 10⁻¹³. How many times is silver benzoate more soluble in a buffer of pH 3.19 compared to its solubility in pure water ?
explanation:
Suppose S is the molar solubility of silver benzoate in water , then  
CHCOOAg    ⇌   CHCOO⁻(aq) + Ag⁺
Ksp = S² , S = √ 2.5 × 10⁻¹³ = 50 × 10⁻⁷ M
If the solubility of salt of weak acid of ionization constant Ka is S , then Ksp, Ka, S' are related to each other at pH = 3.19 
 → [H] = 6.46 × 10⁻⁴
Ksp = S'²[ Ka/(Ka + [H⁺] ]
S' = { 2.5 × 10⁻¹³/ [6.46 × 10⁻⁵/ (6.45 × 10⁻⁵ + 6.46 × 10⁻⁴)]}½
S' = ( 2.75 × 10⁻¹²)½ = 1.658 × 10⁻⁶ M

The ratio S'/S = 1.658 × 10⁻⁶/5 × 10⁻⁷ = 3.32
silver benzoate is 3.32 times more soluble in buffer of pH 3.19 than in pure water.

question: Calculate the pH of the resultant mixtures: 10 mL. of 0.2 M Ca(OH)₂ + 25 mL of 0.1 M HCl

25 mL of 0.1 M HCl = 25 × 0.1 millimoles = 2.5 millimoles of HCl

1 millimole of Ca(OH)₂ reacts with 2 millimoles of HCL

[OH-] = 2 × 0.0214 M = 0.0428 M = 4.28 × 10-²M

pH = 14-1.37 = 12.63.

Initial       4             4               0             0

question:
Does the number of moles of reaction products increase, decrease or remain same when each of the following equilibria is subjected to a decrease in pressure by increasing the volume ?
(a) PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂
(b) CaO(s) + CO₂(g) ⇌ CaCO₃(s)
(c) 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) ⇌ Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g)
explanation: Applying Le Chatelier’s principle, on decreasing the pressure, equilibrium shifts to the direction in which pressure increases, i.e., number of moles of gaseous substances is more. Thus, moles of reaction products will increase in reaction (a), decrease in reaction (b) and remain same (np, = nr gaseous) in reaction (c).

question:
At 1127 K and 1 atmosphere pressure, a gaseous mixture of CO and CO₂ in equilibrium with solid carbon has 90.55% by mass.
C(s) + CO₂(g) ⇌ 2CO(g)
Calculate K꜀ for the reaction at the above temperature.
explanation:
Lets the total mass of the mixture of CO and CO₂ is 100g , then CO = 90.55 g and CO₂ = 100-90.55 = 9.45g 

Moles of CO = 90.55/28 = 3.234
Moles of CO₂ = 9.45/44 = 0.215

Mole fraction of CO = 3.234/(3.234+0.215) = 0.938
Mole fraction of CO₂ = 0.215/(3.234+0.215) = 0.062

→ P(CO) = Mole fraction × Total pressure
                 =  0.938 × 1atm = 0.938 atm
P(CO₂) = 0.062 × 1atm = 0.062 atm
Kₚ for the reaction C(s) + CO₂(g) ⇌ 2CO(g)

Kₚ = P²(CO)/P(CO₂) = (0.938)²/0.062 = 14.19 

△ng = 2-1 = 1 , Kₚ = K꜀(RT)^△ng
K꜀ = Kₚ/(RT) = 14.19/0.0821 × 1127 = 0.153
topic_name: Physical Chemistry >> Equilibrium >> NCERT Exercise

question:
Bromine monochloride (BrCl) decomposes into bromine and chlorine and reaches the equilibrium :
2BrCl(g) ⇌ Br₂(g) + Cl₂(g)
For which K꜀ is 32 at 500 K. If initially pure BrCl is present at a concentration of 3.3× 10⁻³ mol /L, what is its molar concentration in the mixture at equilibrium ?
explanation:
2BrCl(g) ⇌ Br₂(g) + Cl₂(g)
Initial.       3.3 × 10⁻³          0            0
At eq.      3.3 × 10⁻³ - x.      x/2         x/2

K꜀ = (x/2)(x/2) / (3.3 × 10⁻³ - x)² = 32(Given) 
By solving, x = 3 × 10⁻³

At equilibrium, [ BrCl ] = 3.3 × 10⁻³ - 3.0 × 10⁻³ = 3 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L

question: Equilibrium constant K꜀ for the reaction, N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at 500 K is 0.061. At particular time, the analysis shows that the composition of the reaction mixture is : 3.0 mol /L of N₂ , 2.0 mol /L of H₂,0.50 mol /L of NH₃. Is the reaction at equilibrium ? If not, in which direction does the reaction tend to proceed to reach the equilibrium ?
explanation:
Q꜀ = [NH₃]²/[N₂][H₂]³ = (0.5)²/3(0.2)³ = 0.0104
Given K꜀ = 0.061 
As Q꜀ ≠ K꜀ , reaction is not in equilibrium .
As Q꜀ < K꜀ , reaction will proceed in the forward reaction.
topic_name: Physical Chemistry >> Equilibrium >> NCERT Exercise

question:
One of the reactions that takes place in producing steel from iron ore is the reduction of iron (II) oxide by carbon monoxide to give iron metal and CO₂
FeO(s) + CO(g) ⇌ Fe(s) + CO₂(g); Kₚ = 0.265 atm at 1050 K
What are the equilibrium partial pressures of CO and CO₂ at 1050 K if the initial pressures are :Pco = 1.4 atm and Pco₂ = 0.80 atm ?
explanation:
FeO(s) + CO(g) ⇌ Fe(s) + CO₂(g)
Initial pressure  1.4 atm                             0.80 atm
P at equilibrium 1.4 - p                              0.80+p
→ At equilibrium, PCO₂ = (0.80+p)atm,
PCO = (1.4-p)atm
Kₚ = P(CO₂)/P(CO) => 0.265 = 0.80 + p / 1.4-p 
By solving, P = -0.339 atm

P(CO)eq = 1.4 + 0.339 atm = 1.739 atm
P(CO₂)eq = 1.4 - 0.339 atm = 0.461 atm
topic_name: Physical Chemistry >> Equilibrium >> NCERT Exercise

question:
Kₚ = 0.04 atm at 898 K for the equilibrium shown below. What is the equilibrium concentration of C₂H6 when it is placed in a flask at 4 atm pressure and allowed to come to equilibrium.
C₂H₆(g) ⇌ C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g)
explanation:
C₂H₆(g) ⇌ C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g)
Initial pressure 4 atm         0              0
At eqi.                4-p              p              p 
Applying law of Equilibrium,
Kₚ = P(C₂H₆) × P(H₂) / P(C₂H₄) 
0.04 = p²/4-p
p² + 0.04p - 0.16 = 0
→ p = [ - 0.04 ± √ 0.016 - 4(-0.16) ] / 2 = -0.04±0.80/2
Taking positive value, p = 0.76/2 = 0.38 

→ [C₂H₄]eq = 4-0.38 atm = 3.62 atm.

question:
What is the equilibrium concentration of each of the substances in the equilibrium when the initial concentration of ICl was 0.78 M ?

x = 0.292-0.748x

Hence at the equilibrium , [I₂] = [Cl₂] = 0.167 M
[ICl] = 0.78 - 2(0.167) = 0.446 M

question:
Which statement is wrong regarding the conditions to write Lewis-Langmuir theory

a. The Lewis-Langmuir theory can be understood by considering the formation of the chlorine molecule, Cl2. 

b. The Cl atom with electronic configuration, [Ne]3s2 3p5, is one electron short of the Neon configuration.

c. The formation of the Cl2 molecule can be understood in terms of the transfering of a pair of electrons from the one chlorine to another atom, each chlorine atom contributing 8 electrons to the shared pair.

d.  In the process both chlorine atoms attain the outer shell octet of the nearest noble gas (i.e., argon).
explanation:
The Lewis-Langmuir theory can be understood by considering the formation of the chlorine molecule, Cl2. 

The Cl atom with electronic configuration, [Ne]3s2 3p5, is one electron short of the argon configuration. 

The formation of the Cl2 molecule can be understood in terms of the sharing of a pair of electrons between the two chlorine atoms, each chlorine atom contributing one electron to the shared pair. 

In the process both chlorine atoms attain the outer shell octet of the nearest noble gas (i.e., argon). 

Reference: (NCERT chemistry Class 11; page 102; paragraph no.4)

question:
Which statement is wrong regarding the covalent bonding:

a. When two atoms share two electron pair they are said to be joined by a single covalent bond.

b. If two atoms share two pairs of electrons, the covalent bond between them is called a double bond.

c. In the carbon dioxide molecule, we have two double bonds between the carbon and oxygen atoms. Similarly in ethyne molecule the two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond.
explanation:
When two atoms share one electron pair they are said to be joined by a single covalent bond. 

In many compounds we have multiple bonds between atoms. The formation of multiple bonds envisages sharing of more than one electron pair between two atoms. 

If two atoms share two pairs of electrons, the covalent bond between them is called a double bond. 

For example, in the carbon dioxide molecule, we have two double bonds between the carbon and oxygen atoms. 

Similarly in ethene molecule the two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond.  

Reference: (NCERT chemistry Class 11; page 102; paragraph no.6)

question: Which one have odd electron system?
explanation:
